title: Opus5.5 Low to Max - Now in Three.JS ( you guys asked for this)
author: 314t
selftext:
you guys asked for this

We did low to max in godot. 

We did low to max in unreal. 

Now we have low to max in three.js.

What should we do next?

comments.author: 314t
comments.body:
I never let it generate assets in the same run as the build phase, but its allowed to search for existing assets. Assets it cannot find, those I have claude create in their own sessions.  
  
  
\# Cyberpunk Alley Diorama

\## Working rules for this run

\- We are going to build a Three.js project, in this folder. Node.js 24 and npm are installed.

\- Run everything headless where possible.

\- Capture screenshots as needed to verify the visuals.

\- Use retrieved 3D assets (download free, properly licensed models, textures and HDRIs). Do not hand-roll assets: no hand-built procedural stand-ins for props or set dressing.

\- \[library path\] may have existing assets you can reuse (see its library folder and its AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md). Check there before downloading. Copy anything you use into this project; do not modify \[library path\].

\## Brief

Build a moody Three.js diorama: overgrown cyberpunk alley at blue hour, rain-slicked PBR surfaces, neon emissive signs with bloom, volumetric fog, screen-space global illumination (SSGI), ACES tonemapping, tilt-shift depth of field, scattered set dressing, low-angle hero shot.

comments.author: 314t
comments.body: Correct- most assets were downloaded from the internet, if it cannot find one its allowed to search for one. If it cannot find anything on the internet, its told to never make an asset. Asset creation happens in its own session, to not rot the context of the agent building the scene.
